classification.difficultyReason: Select the overlap for school and work, sum all four regions for the denominator, and round the resulting probability to three decimal places.

content.prompt:
Zilda took a survey of eighteen year olds, asking if they work, go to school, do both or neither. The Venn diagram shows the results.

What is the probability that a person randomly selected goes to school and works, rounded to three decimal places?

spec.description: Unshaded overlapping circles inside a rectangular universal-set frame; Work is on the left and School on the right.
spec.mathematics: Work only 19; Work and School 3; School only 16; neither 7. Total 45.
spec.answerVisibility: All four counts and both set labels are permanent student-visible givens; the probability is answer-only.

answer.worked:
There are $3$ people who go to school and work.

$$\begin{align*}
\text{Total surveyed} &= 19+3+16+7 \\
&=45 \\
P(\text{school and work}) &= \frac{3}{45} \\
&\approx 0.067
\end{align*}$$

Rounded to three decimal places.
